summary: Defines a MIB extension to the GBOND-MIB module with objects for managing ATM-based multi-pair bonded xDSL interfaces, as described in ITU-T Recommendation G.998.1. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: Old-style ATM data can ride over bundled phone wires too. This memo gives standard dials for managing such bundles.

questions: what is differential delay in dsl bonding
subtitle: SNMP objects for managing ATM-based bonded DSL links that combine several phone lines into one.

tldr.problem: G.Bond/ATM (ITU-T G.998.1) bundles up to 32 xDSL lines or bearer channels into one logical ATM link, and operators need a standard way to configure and monitor such a bundle.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the G9981-MIB module, which adds port configuration, status, notification and performance-monitoring objects on top of the common GBOND-MIB.
tldr.outcome: The module focuses on differential delay and lost ATM cells, and it must be used together with GBOND-MIB.

today: RFC 6768 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Bonding ATM Over xDSL
sections.content:
G.Bond/ATM, specified in ITU-T Recommendation G.998.1, bonds (aggregates) multiple xDSL lines, or individual bearer channels in those lines, into a single bidirectional logical link that carries an ATM stream. The RFC describes it as an evolution of the older Inverse Multiplexing for ATM (IMA) technology, applied to xDSL with variable rates on each line or channel. Up to 32 individual sub-layers can be bonded.

RFC 6768 defines a MIB module, G9981-MIB, for managing such bonded interfaces. It extends the common objects of the GBOND-MIB module from RFC 6765. The module follows the Internet-Standard Management Framework (RFC 3410) and the SMIv2 rules (RFC 2578, RFC 2579, RFC 2580), and it uses the Broadband Forum report TR-159 as its management model.
sections.eli5: Several thin phone wires are tied together to act like one fat pipe. This memo lists the gauges and switches an operator can use to watch that bundle.

sections.title: Relationship to Other MIB Modules
sections.content:
A G.Bond/ATM port is a special case of a bonded multi-pair xDSL interface, so it is managed through the generic interface objects of the IF-MIB (RFC 2863). An ifIndex identifies G.Bond/ATM ports as well as the xDSL lines and channels beneath them.

The GBOND-MIB (RFC 6765) holds the objects common to all bonded multi-pair xDSL interfaces, such as bonding management and port and channel configuration. Both GBOND-MIB and G9981-MIB are REQUIRED to manage a G.Bond/ATM port. The ATM-MIB (RFC 2515) can be used for the ATM aspects of the port.
sections.eli5: This memo is an add-on page to a bigger manual. You need the main manual and this page together.

sections.title: MIB Structure
sections.content:
All objects live in one group, g9981Port, structured as recommended by RFC 4181. It has four sub-groups:

  • g9981PortNotifications: notifications that an upstream or downstream differential delay tolerance was exceeded.
  • g9981PortConfTable: configuration of a port.
  • g9981PortStatTable: overall status, complementing the IF-MIB ifTable and the GBOND-MIB gBondFltStatus.
  • g9981PM: historical performance monitoring, complementing the GBOND-MIB gBondPortPM.

Other port settings, capabilities and notifications for the Generic Bonding Sub-layer (GBS) stay in GBOND-MIB. The module is registered as object identifier 208 in the mib-2 tree. The RFC also maps its objects to TR-159 managed objects; some of the mapping is not one-to-one, which the RFC calls a partial mapping.
sections.eli5: The dials are grouped into four drawers: alarms, settings, current readings and history.

sections.title: Configuration, Status and Notifications
sections.content:
The configuration table has three read-write objects: g9981PortConfUpDiffDelayTolerance and g9981PortConfDnDiffDelayTolerance, the maximum tolerated upstream and downstream differential delay among the member channels (range 0 to 2047 milliseconds), and g9981PortConfDiffDelayToleranceExceededEnable, which turns the notifications on or off. These are read-write for GBS-C (central office side) ports and irrelevant for GBS-R (remote side) ports, where an attempt to read or change them MUST be rejected with inconsistentValue. Entries in this table MUST be maintained in a persistent manner.

The status table is live data and is not persistent. It reports lost ATM cells seen in the receive direction (g9981PortStatRxLostCells), lost cells seen by the peer port (g9981PortStatTxLostCells), and the current maximum upstream and downstream differential delay across all operational channels, in units of 0.1 ms.

The two notifications, g9981UpDiffDelayToleranceExceeded and g9981DnDiffDelayToleranceExceeded, MAY be sent for GBS-C ports while the port is up, when the delay crosses the threshold in either direction.
sections.eli5: Wires in a bundle can deliver data at slightly different speeds. You set how much lateness is okay, and the device tells you when the gap gets too big.

sections.title: Performance Monitoring
sections.content:
Performance monitoring is OPTIONAL and uses the 64-bit textual conventions from the HC-PerfHist-TC-MIB (RFC 3705), which extend the 32-bit ones in RFC 3593. The module tracks lost cells in each direction and the maximum upstream and downstream differential delay.

Current tables cover the running 15-minute and 1-day intervals. History tables keep up to 96 intervals of 15 minutes (a 900-second interval) and up to 7 one-day intervals (86400 seconds); only interval 1 is required, and intervals 2 to 96 and 2 to 7 are OPTIONAL. The agent SHOULD align each interval with a fifteen-minute boundary of the wall clock, and each one-day interval with the start of a day.

Counters are not reset when a GBS is re-initialized, only when the agent is reset or re-initialized. Counting for certain events is inhibited during Severely Errored Seconds (SES) or Unavailable Seconds (UAS), as each object's description states. If a history bucket is invalid, the BTU MUST NOT produce notifications based on its counters.
sections.eli5: The device keeps a diary: one page for every quarter hour for a day, and one page per day for a week.

sections.title: Conformance
sections.content: An implementation must comply with the IF-MIB (ifCompliance3) and GBOND-MIB (gBondCompliance) compliance statements. In this module, three groups are mandatory: the basic status group, the alarm configuration group and the notification group. The current, 15-minute and 1-day performance groups are required only for implementations that support those kinds of performance monitoring.
sections.eli5: A device must at least have the basic gauges and alarm settings. The diary pages are extras.

sections.title: Security
sections.content:
Changing the configuration table MAY lead to a potential Service Level Agreement breach, for example if a higher delay tolerance increases traffic delay, or if the notifications are disabled. Readable objects can also reveal aspects of interface performance and configuration, so even GET and NOTIFY access should be controlled.

Implementations SHOULD provide the SNMPv3 security features, and deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED. Implementations claiming SNMPv3 compliance MUST fully support authentication and privacy with the User-based Security Model (RFC 3414) and the AES cipher (RFC 3826). They MAY also support the Transport Security Model (RFC 5591) over SSH (RFC 5592) or TLS/DTLS (RFC 6353).
sections.eli5: Turning the dials the wrong way could make the service worse, and the readings are private, so only the right people should be allowed to use them.
